name: Hawaii Department of Health, Clean Water Branch: water quality advisories and events (eha-cloud portal API)
operator: Hawaii Department of Health, Clean Water Branch
waters_covered: statewide coastal waters, streams and harbors; all islands
access_detail: The public portal https://eha-cloud.doh.hawaii.gov/cwb/ calls api/events. A GET with the header 'Accept: application/json' returns JSON {page, totalResultsCount, list} (without it, an HTML snapshot). No key. It returns the newest 500 of 1,901 events (2023-01-01 to 2026-11-07 on 2026-11-07); the page, skip and take parameters are ignored, so older history is not read. createdBy and updatedBy hold the Department's staff e-mail addresses and are never read. E-mail notifications by island through the portal's subscription form.

sample_record.title: Wastewater Discharge at Kalama Park, Kihei, Maui
sample_record.description: Event: Discharge of wastewater from a manhole / Location: Kihei Pump Station #6 ... / Volume: Undetermined / Status of spill: Ongoing / Affected waters: Beach fronting Kalama Park / Warning signs have been posted. The public is advised to remain out of the affected waters until this advisory has been cancelled.

fills_event_fields: valid_until / ended_at of the advisory (closedDate, signRemovalDate)
cannot_fill: spill start time as a field (sometimes in text)
cadence: Posted by the Department as notices are issued (the newest, 2026-11-07 01:24 UTC, hours before the read). Median days from posting to cancellation in the newest 500: Sewage Spill 6.7 (n=50), Permit Exceedance 4.3 (n=14), Brown Water Advisory 7.9 (n=261), Beach Advisory 4.9 (n=50), Beach Notification 1.0 (n=104).
history: 1,901 events in all on 2026-11-07; the endpoint returns the newest 500 (2023-01-01 to 2026-11-07). Types in the newest 500 (read 2026-11-07): Brown Water Advisory 279, Beach Notification 104, Beach Advisory 52, Sewage Spill 50, Permit Exceedance 15; 21 open.
legal_basis: HAR 11-62 Appendix B (wastewater spills, overflows and discharges); HAR 11-55 NPDES
status_reason: Read every refresh by the Hawaii ingester: sewage spill and permit exceedance advisories are sewage reports in the Department's own window (posted to cancelled); Brown Water Advisories are rainfall advisories, a separate category; beach advisories are beach advisories and retest notifications get the site's sample caution. Places are read by rules from the notices' text, per island; no coordinates.
notes: Undocumented API behind a public page; descriptionHtml contains links. Titles sometimes carry a street address. Times (read 2026-11-07): postedDate, closedDate, createdOn and updatedOn are UTC without a zone mark; signRemovalDate is closedDate in Hawaii time; postedDateHst is the UTC date, not the Hawaii date. Some sewage notices give a street address with a house number (removed by the ingester).

name: HAR 11-62 Appendix B: Responses for Wastewater Spills, Overflows, and Discharges (July 1, 2014)
status_reason: Read 2026-11-07 in the Department's copy of chapter 11-62 (effective 2016-03-21). For a spill into state waters the owner or its agent shall immediately notify the CWB, immediately send a press release for spills of 1,000 gallons or more (or lesser ones that threaten public health) to AP, newspapers, TV, the Department's Communications Office and the CWB, immediately post warning signs where public access is possible (the director authorizes removal), monitor the receiving water (enterococci; Clostridium perfringens in fresh or brackish water) until told to stop, and report in writing within five working days. Section 4 (spills onto the ground where the public has or may have access): for 1,000 gallons or more the owner or agent immediately notifies the Wastewater Branch (Oahu) or the district EHP chief, sends the same press release and posts warning signs in the vicinity; smaller ground spills go in a quarterly tabulated summary.
